# Coverage roadmap

This is the forward view of "a reasonable subset of R": which idioms are in,
which are next, and — crucially — the **enabler** each gap needs. It complements
the [grammar coverage map](r-subset-grammar.md), which reports what the compiler
accepts *today* (computed by probing the frontend).

```{r}
cov <- tccquickr:::tccq_grammar_coverage()
counts <- table(factor(cov$disposition, levels = c("core", "boundary", "rejected")))
```

Today: **`r counts[["core"]]` core**, **`r counts[["boundary"]]` boundary**,
**`r counts[["rejected"]]` rejected** of the probed productions.

## The organizing idea

Most missing idioms are blocked by one of a small number of *enablers*. Adding an
enabler unlocks a whole group, so the roadmap is ordered by enabler, not by
surface syntax.

| Enabler | Unlocks | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Elementwise producer / fold IR | arithmetic, comparisons, reducers, `ifelse()` | **done** |
| Scalar conditional node | `if/else`, `ifelse()` | **done** |
| Counted-loop statement + indexed writes | `for`, matrix kernels (Viterbi) | **done** |
| **Loop-carried mutable locals** | `while`, `repeat`, `next`, `break`, accumulator `for` | next |
| **Branch type promotion** | mixed-type `if`/`ifelse` branches | next |
| **Statement-position `if`** | guarded assignment inside loops | next |
| **List type** | `Map`, `lapply`, character `switch` | later |
| **Character/string type** | character `switch`, string ops | later |
| **Dynamic-length output** | `Filter`, `which`, growth patterns | later |

## Control flow

- `for` (counted), scalar `if/else`, and vectorized `ifelse()` are **core**.
- `while` / `repeat` / `next` / `break` need **loop-carried mutable locals**:
  today rebinding a local is rejected, so a loop cannot carry an accumulator.
  The work is (1) relax the rebind rule into an explicit update with a stable
  type, (2) a `while`/`repeat` loop IR node with a re-evaluated condition, and
  (3) `break`/`continue` lowering. This is the single highest-value enabler.
- `switch`: the integer-position form (`switch(i, a, b, c)`) lowers to nested
  conditionals and is tractable now; the character form needs a string type.

## Functional idioms

- `Reduce(FUN, x)` already lowers for **recognized reducer operators**
  (`+`, `*`, `&`, `|`, `min`, `max`). Generalizing to an arbitrary scalar `FUN`
  needs inlining a user closure into the fold body — a frontend/IR extension, not
  a new runtime.
- `vapply()` / `sapply()` over an elementwise scalar `FUN` map cleanly onto the
  **producer** model (the result is a vector) and are the most compilable of the
  apply family.
- `Map()` / `lapply()` return **lists**, so they wait on a list type.
- `Filter()` / `Position()` / `Find()` need **dynamic-length output** (runtime
  compaction), a different storage pattern than the fixed-extent kernels today.

## Type-system extensions (unlock the "later" rows)

- **Lists** — `Map`, `lapply`, character `switch`, struct-of-arrays returns.
- **Character/strings** — character `switch`, `match`, string predicates.
- **Branch type promotion** — a small, local change (promote `if`/`ifelse`
  branches to a common type) that removes the current same-type restriction.

## How this list stays honest

Every "done" row above is backed by a `core` row in the
[grammar coverage map](r-subset-grammar.md) and a differential test against R
([conformance](conformance.md)). When an enabler lands, the coverage map flips
the relevant rows automatically — this roadmap is the plan, that map is the
proof.
